entries.title: Kuva Weapons Overview
entries.summary: Where they come from, what they have, how they grow

blocks.text: Each of these is worth another round of guessing.

These 13 <hl>Kuva weapons</hl> come only from a successful hunt on the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} boss. They are special melee weapons, Tenno, each with its own passive, and each rolls a random <t>weapon level</t> and <t>innate element</t>.

blocks.caption: All 13 of them; see [[weapons/weapon_list]] for each one

blocks.text: How to get one

items: Finish off a {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling} and your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} is born; then build decryption progress from {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}s and unlock the three Requiem cards of the answer. See [[requiem/decryption]]
Place the three cards in the right order in a {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate}; see [[requiem/requiem_gate]]

Hunt down your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}. Only a fully correct card order counts as a success, and a success drops the Kuva weapon in its hand, along with a {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary} and other rewards

The weapon type, level and element are all settled when the Larvling appears: the type picked from the 13 at equal odds, the level inside your current personal level range, the element one of 7. The downed Larvling reveals them, and once your Lich is born the [[requiem/lich_archive|Lich Profile]] shows them too. The range only rises after the drop; see [[weapons/weapon_level]]

blocks.text: <dim>Look up Thralls, decryption and Requiem cards in the [[start/glossary|Glossary]].</dim>

Each Lich of the Origin System carries one of those <x>red-- those RED--</x> those weapons of its own, and once you defeat it, Operator, the weapon is yours, which seems only fair. Each one also comes with an extra elemental damage bonus.
Every one has

rows: Different per weapon; changes with weapon level
Fixed per weapon; does not change with level
Exactly 100% on 95% of weapons, otherwise random between 80% and 120%
Equal to the weapon level as a percentage, so level 40 gives +40%; see [[combat/elements]]

blocks.text: How they get stronger

items: Raise the level: the higher the level, the stronger the weapon. Keep duplicate Kuva weapons, since fusing two raises the level; see [[weapons/weapon_level]]
Install mods: here a mod is a card you slot into a weapon to add stats, not a Minecraft mod. Kuva weapons come pre-consecrated and take mods right away; see [[weapons/weapon_table]]
Swap the element: fusion can replace the element with the other weapon's; see [[weapons/requiem_evolve]]

blocks.text: Other weapons need a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} to be consecrated first, and can then reroll their base panel with {item:kuvalich:forma}. A Kuva weapon's base panel is fixed, so neither does anything to it.
Build the three workbenches in order

items: {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast}: crafted from a {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate}. It trades three Requiem cards or three mods for a new one and breaks down spare mods; see [[weapons/requiem_recast]]
{item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}: its recipe includes a Requiem Recast and a {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary}. It fuses weapons, consecrates them and rerolls panels; see [[weapons/requiem_evolve]]
{item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table}: its recipe includes a Requiem Forge, a Lich Reliquary and 4 {item:kuvalich:kuva}. It installs and removes mods; see [[weapons/weapon_table]]

blocks.text: Deep intel
{lang:kuvalich.attr.short.damage} below 100% counts squared, so 80% really means ×0.64; see [[combat/damage]].
The 13 Kuva weapons come in two types. The 7 <t>heavy</t> ones hit hard, swing slowly and slow you down while held; the 6 <t>light</t> ones hit softer, swing faster and speed you up.

rows: Bonus damage against targets with 0 armor
Chance of a heavy hit; most damage becomes a 5 s DoT
Kills build charge that empowers jump crits
Hits stack a weakening debuff and deal more damage
Group heal on hit; less environmental damage while held
Bonus damage against 0-armor targets; longer reach
Chance of a heavy hit; charged right-click dash that wrecks everything around
Hits raise attack speed and add a DoT
Lifesteal on hit; charged right-click dash
Every swing lands an extra hit first
Full Viral with a Toxin element; other elements actually lose damage

blocks.text: The {item:kuvalich:kuva_shildeg}, {item:kuvalich:arca_titron}, {item:kuvalich:sancti_magistar} and {item:kuvalich:prisma_veritux} also <t>break shields</t>; hitting a raised shield knocks it out, the way an axe does.

blocks.title: Picking one
blocks.text: No single weapon does it all. For crowds, use the {item:kuvalich:gram_prime} or the {item:kuvalich:pennant}'s charged skill; for high-health targets, the {item:kuvalich:guandao_prime} and the {item:kuvalich:pennant}. For sustain, take the {item:kuvalich:sancti_magistar} or the {item:kuvalich:reaper_prime}, and for farming, the {item:kuvalich:machete}.
Ordis knows a Prime name on sight. In the records, gear with Prime in its name is mostly the Orokin-era version of an existing item, usually with better stats and gold trim.
Attack, speed, movement

The table shows each weapon at exactly the <t>benchmark level</t>, level {cfg:kuva_lich.benchmarkLevel}, and higher levels are stronger; see [[weapons/weapon_level]]. Movement is a percentage of your base speed.
Crit and status

These three belong to the weapon itself and do not change with level; [[start/glossary|mods]] add percentages on top of them. They are a weapon's foundation, Tenno; every bonus you add later is built on them.

rows: Chance to land a critical hit; see [[combat/crit]]
How much a crit multiplies the physical damage
Chance for a hit to trigger an elemental effect; see [[combat/element_status]]

blocks.text: Full passive numbers for every weapon are in [[weapons/heavy_weapons]] and [[weapons/light_weapons]].

entries.title: Weapon Level & Caps
entries.summary: How level shapes power and how it rises

blocks.text: How strong a Kuva weapon is comes down almost entirely to its <hl>weapon level</hl>, and every one has it. The level is the number at the end of the “{lang:kuvaweapon.type} element level” line right under the name in the tooltip.
What a level is worth

The <t>benchmark level</t> {cfg:kuva_lich.benchmarkLevel} is the dividing line. Each level above it adds {cfg:kuva_weapon.attributeMultiplier|pctv} of the benchmark value to stats like attack damage, and each level below takes the same amount away.
Level factor L = (weapon level − {cfg:kuva_lich.benchmarkLevel}) ÷ 100 × {cfg:kuva_weapon.attributeMultiplier}

rows: Heavy weapons slow you less as level rises, but never speed you up; light weapons speed you up more, but never slow you down
Most multipliers, radii and durations are multiplied by (1+L) or part of it; see [[weapons/heavy_weapons]] and [[weapons/light_weapons]]
Equal to the weapon level as a percentage, regardless of the benchmark; see [[combat/elements]]

blocks.text: Below level {cfg:kuva_lich.benchmarkLevel}, L is negative, so attack, speed and passives are all discounted, and a passive that says “damage ×1.25” can even end up reducing damage. The lower the level, the worse it gets. Check the level before you pick your main weapon, Tenno.
Level colors
Your level range

The weapon your Lich drops has its level rolled between your personal <t>floor and ceiling</t> the moment the Larvling appears, and the downed Larvling shows it. The range belongs to your character and survives death; a new character starts at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.baseMinimumLevel}–{cfg:kuva_lich.baseMaximumLevel}</t>.

items: After a successful hunt on your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}, the drop's level is rolled from your current range first
Then a number from {cfg:kuva_lich.minimumLevelCapIncrease}–{cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevelCapIncrease} is rolled and added to floor and ceiling at once; chat tells you the new values
The floor stops at {cfg:kuva_lich.minimumLevel} and the ceiling at {cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevel}; once capped they no longer rise

blocks.text: So your first successful hunt drops a weapon between level <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.baseMinimumLevel}</t> and <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.baseMaximumLevel}</t>. After that, floor and ceiling rise by the same number, so the whole range shifts upward; once one end is capped, only the other keeps rising.
Only [[weapons/requiem_evolve|fusion]] takes a weapon past level {cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevel}, up to level {cfg:kuva_lich.upgradeLimit}.
Deep intel
Kuva weapons in the Creative inventory roll their level from a new character's starting range, not from your current personal range.

entries.title: Requiem Recast
items: kuvalich:requiem_recast

blocks.text: Trades at this workbench have no confirm step, so all three cards are gone the moment the third goes in. Think before you place it, Tenno. The {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast} is the first of the three workbenches to build. It trades three Requiem cards or three [[start/glossary|mods]] for a new one, and breaks spare mods down into {item:kuvalich:endo}.
Endo is the material for upgrading mods; see [[modules/module_level]].
It has 3 input slots at the bottom and 1 output slot at the top. Fill all three, or put in a single mod, and the result appears on its own; there is no button.
Card 3-in-1
Any 3 Requiem cards, worn ones included, make 1 random new card at full durability, with each of the 8 kinds equally likely. For how cards are used, see [[requiem/requiem_cards]].
All three are consumed the instant the third one goes in, and the new card appears in the output.
Mod 3-in-1

3 mods make 1 <t>unrevealed mod</t>, and three of one rarity give that rarity; right-click it in your main hand to reveal it. These are also spent as soon as all three are in, and weapon and Warframe mods can't be mixed.

items: 3 weapon mods of one tier, whether Bronze, Silver or Gold

items.text: Bronze, Silver and Gold weapon mods can be mixed, but Prime and Riven cannot. The output tier is rolled by the ratio you put in, so 2 Gold + 1 Bronze gives Gold about 2/3 of the time and Bronze 1/3
3 Warframe mods of one tier, whether Bronze, Silver or Gold; see [[warframe/warframe_module]]
Bronze, Silver and Gold Warframe mods can be mixed, but Prime and Riven cannot; the output tier is rolled by ratio the same way

blocks.text: Breaking mods into Endo

Put in a single weapon or Warframe mod and the output slot previews how much {item:kuvalich:endo} it is worth. The mod is only consumed when you take the Endo out; if you change your mind, take the mod back.

rows: +1 per cycle done; unrevealed Rivens count as 0

blocks.text: Taking any amount of Endo out of the output slot counts as breaking the mod down.
Crafting
Crafting it uses up a {item:kuvalich:requiem_gate}, and mining it back takes a diamond pickaxe.

entries.title: Requiem Forge
items: kuvalich:requiem_evolve

blocks.text: In a fusion the left weapon stays and the middle one is gone, so don't swap them. The {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} is the core weapon workbench: fusing two Kuva weapons, consecrating ordinary weapons so they can take mods, and rerolling panels with Forma all happen here.

items: Right-click to open it; the <t>left slot</t> takes what you are working on and the <t>middle slot</t> the material
With the right combination, the result appears in the <t>right slot</t> on its own; there is no button
Take the result out of the right slot and you are done

rows: Fusion, which can raise the level and swap the element
Consecration, after which it can take mods

cells: Permanently raises the gun's damage; see [[tacz/tacz_enhance]]

blocks.text: Riven rerolls are paid per preview. Each preview costs its Kuva and adds 1 to that Riven's cycle count, and changing the material slot after a preview previews again and charges again. Close the screen or pull the material out without taking the result, and the Kuva already paid is not refunded.
Weapon fusion
New level = round down[ higher of the two levels × {cfg:kuva_lich.upgradeMultiplier|add:1} ], max {cfg:kuva_lich.upgradeLimit}

items: The result is the left weapon, which keeps its weapon type, base panel and installed mods
<w>Its element is replaced by the middle weapon's</w>
The middle weapon disappears along with every mod on it, so remove good mods at the [[weapons/weapon_table]] first
The two can be different Kuva weapons
Close the screen without taking the result and both weapons come back

blocks.text: Your main weapon always goes on the left, and to change its element, put the weapon carrying the element you want in the middle. If you only want a higher level, it doesn't matter where the higher-level one sits, since the new level uses the higher of the two.

The ship's records describe Valence Fusion, in which two copies of the same Kuva weapon become one. The higher of the two elemental bonuses is kept and raised by 10%, up to 60%, and you choose which of the two elements stays.
Consecration
Put any single sword, axe, bow, crossbow or similar item on the left and a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver} in the middle, and the item instantly rolls a random base panel; after that it can take mods.
Each item can be consecrated only once. If you don't like the panel, reroll it with Forma; see [[weapons/forma]].
Crafting
It needs a {item:kuvalich:requiem_recast} and a {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary}, so you need at least one successful hunt first. It is very hard, and mining it back takes a diamond pickaxe.
Deep intel
Fusion drops fractions, so at very low levels, where level × {cfg:kuva_lich.upgradeMultiplier|pct} is under 1, fusing adds no level at all but still swaps the element.

entries.title: Weapon Arsenal
items: kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table

blocks.text: The {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table} installs and removes <hl>mods</hl>. A mod is a card you slot into a weapon to add stats, and every weapon has 8 slots.
Mods travel with the weapon. They are stored on it, so once installed they work wherever it goes; the workbench stores nothing.

items: Right-click to open it and put a <t>consecrated</t> weapon in the weapon slot at the bottom. Only consecrated weapons take mods; Kuva weapons come pre-consecrated, and other weapons get consecrated at the [[weapons/requiem_evolve]] first
The 8 mod slots above become usable and show the mods already on the weapon
Drop a mod into an empty slot to install it and take it out to remove it; <g>nothing is consumed</g>
Take the weapon out or close the screen and it returns to your inventory with its mods; if your inventory is full it drops at your feet

rows: Revealed weapon mods; Warframe mods go to [[warframe/warframe_table]]
No two of the same mod, and conflicting mods cannot be installed together
Mods jump to the first slot that accepts them; consecrated weapons jump to the weapon slot
Opens the weapon mod Codex; see [[modules/module_codex]]

blocks.text: Mods whose names start with “Unveiled” haven't been revealed yet; right-click one in your main hand first, then install it.
Operator, the Arsenal here takes its name from the loadout station on a Tenno's ship, where mods for Warframes and weapons go in and out. Ordis keeps that station spotless.
Mod rarity and stacking rules are in [[modules/module_overview]], and limits on mods in [[modules/module_limits]].
Crafting
Crafting it takes 4 {item:kuvalich:kuva}, 1 {item:kuvalich:lich_reliquary} and a {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}, so you need one successful hunt first. Mining it back takes a diamond pickaxe.

entries.title: Reading the Weapon Panel
entries.summary: Tooltip groups and what each key shows

blocks.text: Learn to read the panel first. Hover over any <t>consecrated</t> item, the kind that can take mods, to see its <hl>weapon panel</hl>, a list of the weapon's current stats. Kuva weapons come pre-consecrated.
A Kuva weapon's panel has an extra top line, “{lang:kuvaweapon.type} element level”. The element name is in its element color and the level number uses the [[weapons/weapon_level|level colors]].
No mods installed

You see only four base values, {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.damage}, {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.criticalStrikeProbability}, {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.criticalStrikeMultiplier} and {lang:kuvalich.attr.short.triggerChance}. For Kuva weapons, see [[weapons/weapon_list]]; other weapons roll them when consecrated, with the odds in [[weapons/forma]].
With mods

rows: Your final panel with mods applied; Crit Chance and Crit Damage are shown as “melee / ranged”
Stacks, current bonus and state of each kill stack; see [[combat/kill_stack]]
Status share of each element and total elemental damage; see [[combat/elements]]
All other attributes, with firearm attributes hidden on melee weapons by default; see [[reference/weapon_attr_damage]]

cells: Bonuses that mods on your other gear give your main-hand weapon, shown only for the main-hand weapon; see [[modules/multi_slot]]

rows: The installed mods, with “installed/8” in the header

blocks.text: A <c:6FD8E8>cyan</c> value is currently raised by kill stacks, and a <c:FF7B7B>red</c> one is negative.
Hold a key

rows: Default view; values include your current kill stacks
Same layout, but values exclude stacks; compare it with the default view to see what the stacks are propping up

cells: Attribute sources, covering what each mod adds, where gear bonuses come from and which attributes were cut off by a cap; see [[modules/module_limits]]
Attribute sources, covering what each mod adds and where gear bonuses come from

rows: Live status: per-stack bonus of each kill stack, how elements combined, how status chance is worked out

blocks.text: When several keys are held, SHIFT wins, then CTRL, then ALT.
“{lang:item.kuvalich.forma_locked}” at the top of the panel means this weapon's base panel is locked; see [[weapons/forma]].
Deep intel

items: In the ALT view, status chance = base × (1 + mods) × (1 + stacks), capped at 500% per hit; above that it is marked “{lang:kuvalich.panel.trigger.capped}”
Panel position, width, density and which groups show can all be changed in your own client settings, and only affect you

entries.title: Forma
entries.summary: Reroll the base panel of non-Kuva weapons
items: kuvalich:forma
kuvalich:shadow_forma

blocks.text: What the new panel turns out to be is pure chance, beyond even my reach, and a bad roll means spending another Forma and trying again. {item:kuvalich:forma} <hl>rerolls the base panel</hl>, rolling a weapon's base damage, crit chance, crit damage and status chance again. It only works on <t>consecrated non-Kuva weapons</t>; consecration is covered in [[weapons/requiem_evolve]].

items: kuvalich:forma
kuvalich:shadow_forma
Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve}
Put the weapon in the left slot, one at a time, and a {item:kuvalich:forma} in the middle
One Forma is spent immediately and the rerolled weapon appears on the right, its installed mods untouched
If you don't like it, put it back on the left and roll again

blocks.text: Forma comes from the Origin System, where it changes the polarity of a mod slot on a weapon. The price is the weapon's rank, which drops to zero, so the weapon has to be leveled all over again.
How the new panel is rolled
Consecration rolls its panel the same way. Almost every roll is Normal; Jackpot and Dud are about 1 in 1000 each.

Within Normal, base damage has a 60% chance to be exactly 100%, and crit chance a 30% chance to become 25%–40% instead. The result is then adjusted once more by how high the crit chance is; see Deep intel at the end.
Base damage below 100% counts squared, so an 80% panel really deals 64% and a Dud's 50% only 25%; see [[combat/damage]].
Panel lock

Every reroll with a normal Forma has a {cfg:kuva_lich.formaLockChance|pctv} chance to permanently lock the weapon. A locked weapon shows “{lang:item.kuvalich.forma_locked}” at the top of its panel, and normal Forma can no longer touch it.
{item:kuvalich:shadow_forma}

items: Used exactly like Forma

items.text: Ignores the lock and removes it after rerolling; it never rolls the lock chance itself

items: No recipe and no drops; it only exists in the Creative inventory

blocks.text: Crafting
Crafts 3 at a time; stacks to 16.
Deep intel

rows: Crit damage becomes 2.5–3.0× and base damage drops to 80%–90%; above 30% crit there is also a 60% chance that status falls to 1%–5%
60% chance of crit damage 2.5–3.0× with base damage 110%–120%; about a 4% chance of crit damage 3.0–3.5× with base damage 70%–80%

entries.summary: Passives and numbers of the 7 heavy weapons

blocks.text: Learn the notation below first, Tenno. All 7 heavy weapon passives are written with it.

rows: Swing only once the attack cooldown bar is full. Unless stated otherwise, passives need a fully charged attack
Level factor, positive above the benchmark level and negative below; see [[weapons/weapon_level]]
Gets only half the level scaling

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:kuva_shildeg}

items: Against targets with <t>0 armor</t>, damage ×1.25×(1+L); a single point of armor cancels the bonus
Breaks shields

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:paracesis}

items: 31% chance for this hit to deal ×2.6
×2 more damage against players
Only <w>30%</w> of the damage lands immediately; the other 70% is multiplied by (1+L) and becomes a 5 s DoT

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:arca_titron}

items: Each kill while holding it adds 1 charge, up to 10, lasting 20×(1+L) s; every kill refreshes the timer, and kills need no full charge
Charge only empowers vanilla jump crits, with crit multiplier ×(1 + stacks×5%×(1+L)). At the benchmark level, 10 stacks turn 1.5 into 2.25
This is separate from the Crit Chance on your panel; ground attacks gain nothing from charge
Breaks shields

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:vitrica}

items: Every hit stacks a debuff on the target, up to 8 stacks, lasting 10×(1+L) s and refreshed on every hit
Each stack gives the target <g>−7.5%</g> attack damage, attack speed, armor, armor toughness and movement speed, for −60% at 8 stacks
This hit deals ×1.25×(1+L/2). The debuff is applied before damage is settled, so even the first hit benefits

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:gram_prime}

items: Attacks at ≥75% charge splash other creatures within about 4×(1+L/6) blocks of the target
Each takes your attack damage ×66%×charge, counting Sharpness-type enchantment bonuses
The splash counts as your melee attack and goes through the weapon panel as usual, so mods, crits and elements all apply
The splash does not pick sides. Pets and villagers standing nearby get hit too, and so do other players when PvP is allowed

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:sancti_magistar}

items: After a hit, heals you and every other player within 15 blocks over 2.5 s, each for a total of this hit's damage ×5%×(1+2L)
<w>On very low-level weapons, once L drops to −0.5 or lower</w>, 1+2L ≤ 0 and nobody is healed at all
While held, <t>damage with no source</t> is reduced by 50%×(1+L/2): falling, burning, lava, drowning, suffocation, Poison and Wither effects and so on
Breaks shields

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:prisma_veritux}

items: Against targets with 0 armor, damage ×1.25×(1+L)
While held, block reach and attack reach each +1×(1+L/2) blocks
Attack speed and movement scale fully with level, while other heavy weapons only get half
Breaks shields

blocks.text: Deep intel

items: The {item:kuvalich:paracesis} DoT starts after 0.25 s and ticks every game tick, straight off the target's health
A jump crit for the {item:kuvalich:arca_titron} means swinging while falling, over 90% charged, and not sprinting
The {item:kuvalich:vitrica} hit deals ×0.75 only when the target has none of the debuff

entries.title: Light Weapons in Detail
entries.summary: Passives and numbers of the 6 light weapons
items: kuvalich:pennant
kuvalich:guandao_prime
kuvalich:reaper_prime
kuvalich:destreza_prime
kuvalich:machete
kuvalich:caustacyst

blocks.text: The 6 light weapon passives use the same notation, L, ×(1+L) and the rest, explained in [[weapons/heavy_weapons]]. Unless stated otherwise, passives need a fully charged attack, so let the attack cooldown bar fill before you swing.
{item:kuvalich:pennant}

items: 32% chance for this hit to deal ×2.4
<hl>Charged right-click</hl>: hold right-click for at least 1 s, then release to dash where you are looking; faster movement means a longer dash
On release, every creature within 12×(1+L/4) blocks of you instantly takes a hit of magic damage that ignores armor, based on 20% of its current health
That hit counts as your attack, goes through the weapon panel as usual and can also roll the 32% heavy hit above, so it usually ends up above 20%
Everything hit then keeps losing health for 5 s based on its missing health, growing heavier as it goes
10 s cooldown. It hits friend and foe alike and only spares you; other players only take damage when PvP is allowed

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:guandao_prime}

items: On hit your attack speed +11%, becoming +16% if you hit again while it lasts; lasts 5×(1+L) s
It also applies a DoT of 20 ticks over 5 s straight off the target's health, totalling (this hit's damage + 2.5% of the target's max health)×(1+L)
Attack damage only gets half the level scaling (1+L/2); attack speed and movement get all of it (1+L)

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:reaper_prime}

items: Lifesteal on hit, healing this hit's damage ×10%×(1+L)
The damage used here is the value before the weapon panel and mods are applied, so stacking damage mods does not raise the heal
<hl>Right-click dash</hl>: hold right-click for at least 0.25 s and release to dash where you look. The longer you hold, the stronger the dash, from 0.5× up to 1.5× at a full 1 s
Distance also scales with your movement speed and (1+L/3). Cooldown is 1.5–4.5 s, longer for stronger dashes, and the dash itself deals no damage

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:destreza_prime}

items: Every attack at ≥66% charge first lands an extra hit, every time, with no chance roll
The extra hit = your attack damage ×33.3%×charge, counting Sharpness-type enchantment bonuses; it also goes through the weapon panel as usual
Attack speed and movement scale fully with level

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:machete}

items: Killing an <t>animal or monster</t> while holding it multiplies each drop stack by a random ×1, ×2 or ×3; no full charge needed
Armor, swords, pickaxes, axes, shovels and hoes are not multiplied
Special drops of the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave} and the {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}, such as Kuva, Riven Slivers and mods, are spawned separately and never multiplied

blocks.text: {item:kuvalich:caustacyst}

items: With a {lang:kuvaweapon.type.poison} innate element, hits apply a full 10 stacks of {lang:kuvaweapon.type.virus}, max health <g>−50%</g>, for 7.5×(1+L) s; damage is unchanged
With any other element, this hit deals ×0.75×(1+L) and applies only 1 Viral stack
Attack speed and movement scale fully with level
To switch to Toxin, put a Toxin Kuva weapon in the middle slot of a fusion ([[weapons/requiem_evolve]]); for Viral effects, see [[combat/element_status]]

blocks.text: Deep intel

items: The {item:kuvalich:pennant}'s follow-up damage ticks every 0.25 s, each tick about 0.46% of missing health at first and up to 2.1% later, ×(1+L)
After the {item:kuvalich:destreza_prime}'s extra hit, the target's hit-immunity window is shortened so your normal attack still connects
The {item:kuvalich:machete} does not multiply drops from Slimes, Magma Cubes, Ghasts, Phantoms, Shulkers, Squid, Villagers and Iron Golems, which count as neither animals nor monsters in game code
The {item:kuvalich:machete} also skips bosses that cannot change dimensions, such as the Wither and the Ender Dragon
